samples.question: This image shows six framed rectangular panels of identical size, numbered 1 to 6 in reading order: panels 1, 2 and 3 are the top row from left to right, and panels 4, 5 and 6 are the bottom row from left to right. Every panel contains exactly five solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, so all six panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink. In each panel the five dots form a lane running from one side of the panel towards the other at that panel's own arbitrary tilt, with irregular spacing between neighbouring dots, so neither the tilt of a lane, the gaps along it, its length, nor its place inside the panel carries any information. Exactly one panel is perfectly straight: the centres of all five of its dots lie on one single straight line. In each of the other five panels the lane is bent, because exactly one of its three inner dots is pushed sideways off the line of the rest, far enough that its centre misses the straight line through the rest of that lane by at least a third of a dot's width. No line is drawn in the image; only the dots and the panel frames are drawn, and straightness must be judged from the dot centres alone. Which numbered panel holds the perfectly straight lane of five dots? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5, panel-6.
